(1) face landmarking is a very challenging task, (2) there exist several landmarking techniques with different properties, and (3) there exist no landmarking techniques that can be considered state-of-the-art.

(1) landmarking performance has increased by an order of magnitude since 2005, (2) the best performance is achieved by the most recent methods and (3) landmarking is now at the stage where it can be deployed in real-life applications.

the best performing landmarking methods are those that are (a) trained on a large number of images with a variety of poses and expressions, (b) use a combination of shape and appearance information, and (c) employ discriminative classifiers.

the detection of a set of 68 facial landmarks, as defined by the 68-point facial landmark model of the 300-W challenge.
the development of a robust face landmarking system that can be used in a variety of applications.
the detection and localization (or “landmarking”) of certain characteristic points (or “landmarks”) on the human face.
